issue_paraphrase: Passing a bounds object built from scalar limits into minimize() silently rewrites that object in place: the scalar lower and upper limits are replaced with arrays broadcast to the size of the current optimization problem, and the flag recording whether bounds may be violated is left in a state tied to the first call. A caller who creates one dimension-agnostic bounds object and reuses it for problems of different sizes gets corrupted limits from the second call onward, and any code that inspects the object afterwards sees data it never assigned.
fix_summary: Shallow-copies the Bounds object in `_validate_bounds` before broadcasting lb/ub onto it, so the caller's instance is never mutated and can be reused across problems of different sizes.

observed_failure_at_parent: ValueError: Hessian evaluated outside domain -- trust-exact constructed and evaluated a full local model (including the Hessian) at the proposed trial point before accepting it, so an out-of-domain trial point aborted the whole optimization instead of shrinking the trust radius
verified: both directions observed in bench-base:python-3.12. At parent a804efa6e (git reset --hard + git clean -fd; source inspected: `_minimize_trust_region` built `m_proposed = subproblem(x_proposed, fun, jac, hess, ...)` and called `m_proposed.fun` before the acceptance ratio) the repro raises ValueError from the Hessian; at fix 34d57a75a (objective evaluated directly at the trial point first, NaN treated as inf/rejected, model built only on acceptance) the repro prints 'True [1.]' and upstream pytest test_trust_exact_rejects_nan_trial_point passes.
install_recipe: pip install . --no-build-isolation (needs full toolchain; see notes)
issue_paraphrase: The trust-region family of minimizers (e.g. trust-exact) evaluates the objective, gradient and Hessian at a proposed trial point before deciding whether to accept the step, and treats a NaN objective at the trial point as an ordinary value. When the objective is only defined on part of the domain, optimization aborts with an exception thrown by an out-of-domain Hessian evaluation instead of rejecting the step and shrinking the search radius, and domain-undefined (NaN) trial values are not handled as rejections either.
fix_summary: Moved the local-model construction to after the trial point is accepted, evaluating the raw objective at the candidate first, and maps NaN objective values at trial points to +inf so the step is rejected and the trust radius shrinks (also cutting wasted Hessian evaluations on rejected steps).
notes: Pure-Python, 26-line delta; requires understanding the trust-region accept/reject iteration. The golden test asserts convergence to x=[1] with tol=1e-8 and success; a fix must both avoid evaluating the Hessian out of domain and reject NaN trials. Optimize tests import cleanly.
